headline: Xbox cuts jobs as Activision takes over Halo
summary: Microsoft announced further Xbox restructuring, with Activision taking over the Halo, Sea of Thieves and Age of Empires franchises and hundreds more job cuts, part of a 'reset' begun in July. Outlets differ on the exact numbers of jobs cut.

claims.statement: Microsoft is cutting roughly 268 more Xbox jobs as part of the restructuring.

sources.quote: Microsoft is also laying off around 268 Xbox employees

claims.statement: Activision will take over the Halo, Sea of Thieves and Age of Empires franchises.

sources.quote: The latest changes will see Activision take on the Halo and Sea of Thieves franchises, as well as Age of Empires.
Call of Duty's Activision to make next Halo game
Activision making the next Halo game

claims.statement: The cuts follow a "reset" of Xbox's gaming business announced in July, when 1,600 employees were laid off.

sources.quote: 1,600 Xbox employees were impacted by layoffs in July
a "reset" announced by Xbox in July

claims.statement: Xbox CEO Asha Sharma described the cuts as "the most significant restructure in Xbox history."

sources.quote: Xbox CEO Asha Sharma describing the cuts as "the most significant restructure in Xbox history."

discrepancies.explanation: The Verge's own headline cites 268 job cuts today while its article text cites around 260.

quotes.quote: Microsoft is laying off around 260 Xbox employees today

discrepancies.explanation: BBC cites 3,600 total planned job losses from the reset, while The Verge cites 3,200 roles.
